patch.value: Source-to-item traceability: derive which tracked work produced any given file or line, so an agent can ask why this code exists and get an evidence-backed answer

Items link forward to the files they touched, but the reverse question - which item, decision, and rationale produced this line - has no answer inside pm. An agent reading unfamiliar code must guess from commit messages, and the decision that justified the code is usually two links away in an ADR that the code does not reference. This feature derives the reverse index from evidence that already exists: linked file paths on items, commit-to-item association, and line attribution from the version control host. Given a path and optional line range it returns the items that touched it, ranked by contribution and recency, each carrying its rationale fields and its path to the governing decision. Derivation is evidence-only: where attribution is ambiguous the answer says so rather than guessing, and nothing is written back onto items as fabricated links.

Given a file path and optional line range, the SDK returns the tracked items associated with it, ranked by contribution and recency, with the evidence that produced each association; Each returned item carries its rationale (value, why-now, outcome) and the shortest typed path to the decision that governs it, so the answer is a why and not just a what; Attribution is derived from existing evidence - linked paths, commit association, and line attribution - and ambiguity is reported explicitly rather than resolved by guessing; The reverse index is bounded and incremental at repository scale, and never blocks a command on a full history scan; The derivation writes no fabricated relationships onto items; any edge it proposes is surfaced as a reviewable suggestion; A CLI surface exposes the query in the target noun grammar, and the answer fits an explicit token budget
Code carries its rationale, retrievable from the tracker without archaeology

Project management equals context management: the context an agent most often lacks when editing unfamiliar code is why the code is the way it is, and that context already exists in the tracker but is only reachable in the forward direction.
Closes the loop between source and rationale, making every file a query into the decision history and giving reviewers and agents an evidence-backed answer instead of a commit-log guess.
A bounded reverse index from paths to tracked work and its governing decisions, derived only from recorded evidence.
Linked-file ownership, evidence-edge reconstruction, and graph path queries have all shipped or are actively owned; the reverse direction is the missing composition and the one agents ask for most.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Traceability coverage measured at build 2026.7.29, and it is complete.

Every source, test and documentation file in the repository is referenced by at least one tracker item: 400 of 400 src TypeScript files, 390 of 390 test spec files, 42 of 42 docs markdown files. Zero unreferenced files in any of the three sets. 1,137 distinct repository paths appear across item files.

Method and its honest limit. The census matches any occurrence of a repository path inside an item's stored document, which includes formal linked-file and linked-doc entries as well as paths named in descriptions, comments and notes. It therefore proves reachability - for any file, some item explains why it exists - but not that every file carries a structured link on the item that owns it. The forward direction this item inverts is the stronger claim; this measurement bounds the reverse direction at 100 percent and tells the eventual gate what its baseline is.

Companion number for the linked-path health check: validate reports 179 missing linked paths against this same corpus, all of which are moved or deleted historical paths on terminal holders, partitioned under pm-zw9188.
